quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting or reacting with anger, what should you do?

options.text: Don't make eye contact.
Don't use hand gestures.
Stay away from the situation.
All of these.

questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, move away from them physically and mentally. Avoid eye contact and don't make gestures that could anger them. Slow down, change lanes, or do whatever is safe to get away from danger.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.
Change lanes quickly.
Speed up quickly.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast on slippery roads is very dangerous. This is even more important when turning. Slow down more than usual when making turns on slippery roads.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate closes.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Ignore how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop. This keeps you safe from trains and other vehicles using the rails.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is safe if you are a good driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds over 80 miles per hour, survival is unlikely. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview and side mirrors to make sure no one is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Merging traffic.
Multiple turns.
Lane shifting.
Do not block intersection.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns you that traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to let them merge safely.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cross traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back.
Keep driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Don't make a sudden turn to catch a missed exit. If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.question: When entering a main road from a private driveway, you must:

options.text: Yield to vehicles already on the main road.
You have the right-of-way.
Enter only if there is a traffic light.
Have someone stop traffic for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to vehicles already on the main road.
questions.explanation: When entering a road from a driveway, alley, parking lot, or roadside, you must yield to vehicles already on the main road.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, not what the flagger says.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow normal traffic laws.

questions.explanation: Slow down and follow directions from signs, flaggers, or police officers in construction zones. Not obeying is illegal and unsafe for workers.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: One-way traffic.
Two-way left turn.
Two-way traffic.
Minimum speed limit.

questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers what they must do. This sign shows you which direction to drive on a one-way street.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when large trucks, buses, and vehicles with trailers turn?

options.text: They always let left-turning traffic go first.
They back up to make room before turning.
They make wide turns and may cross the centerline.
They may stop suddenly during the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make wide turns and may cross the centerline.
questions.explanation: Large trucks, buses, and trailers need extra space to turn. They swing wide and may cross the centerline. Do not crowd the intersection or pass these vehicles, especially on the right side.

questions.question: When riding a bicycle on a sidewalk or in a crosswalk, you should ride slowly and:

options.text: Not warn pedestrians before passing them.
Let pedestrians have the right-of-way.
Take the right-of-way instead of yielding to pedestrians.
Not try to avoid hitting a pedestrian.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists may ride on a sidewalk unless local rules say otherwise. Bicyclists must let pedestrians have the right-of-way on sidewalks and in crosswalks.

questions.question: When you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend, you should:

options.text: Not worry about it because all vehicles are the same.
Not tell your friend that you are not familiar with the vehicle.
Ignore any problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn how to use all the vehicle's equipment before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn how to use all the vehicle's equipment before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, spend a few minutes learning where and how to use the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before driving.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Stay farther behind the vehicle in front of you.
Be careful around all other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: In snowy weather, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead because slippery roads make it harder for your vehicle to stop.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no train in sight or sound, you must stop if:

options.text: A stop sign is posted.
A crossing gate is lowered.
The crossing lights are flashing red.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks if red lights flash, a gate is down, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is close. If you are unsure, stop. Never race a train.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is most likely:

options.text: A deaf person.
Conducting a traffic study.
A blind person.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: You must always let a blind person with a white cane or guide dog cross first. They have the right-of-way.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes because other vehicles could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ can cause a crash.

options.text: Look away from the road
Let go of the steering wheel
Stop focusing on driving
All of the above

questions.explanation: Anything that distracts you from driving is dangerous. This includes looking away from the road, letting go of the wheel, or stopping paying attention to driving.

questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a phone.
Adjusting the radio or CD player.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Drivers must make about 200 decisions per mile, so you need to focus completely on driving. Any extra task can distract you and create danger.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?

options.text: Never put an infant or young child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can hurt an infant or young child, even in a slow crash.
Always make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always wear your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce the risk of injury or death in a crash. Children 12 and under must sit properly restrained in the back seat. Never put a rear-facing infant car seat in the front seat with an airbag.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving?

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
Puts you to sleep.
Wakes you up.
Improves your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your brain activity and reduces your driving skills. It makes your reaction time slower and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: In which ways can alcohol affect you?

options.text: It slows your reaction time.
It gives you false confidence.
It impairs your thinking.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. You may feel overly confident or silly. Alcohol also slows your reaction time, coordination, and balance. It impairs your vision and ability to judge distance, making it hard to respond to what is around you.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Create a routine before you drive. Before you start the car, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Avoid standing water and puddles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car takes longer to stop and may skid when turning. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: You see a "Merging traffic" sign on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Honk at the incoming traffic.
Stay at your current speed.
Speed up to avoid traffic congestion.
Change lanes, if safe, to let traffic merge in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes, if safe, to let traffic merge in.
questions.explanation: When you are on a road with two or more lanes, make room for vehicles entering. If the lane next to you is empty, move over to let them in.
